20. Notice the masochistic tendency of leftist tactics.  Leftists protest
by lying down in front of vehicles, they intentionally provoke police or
racists to abuse them, etc.  These tactics may often be effective, but 
many leftists use them not as a means to an end but because they PREFER 
masochistic tactics.  Self-hatred is a leftist trait.

: Unfortunately, it seems to me that many people who take up a cause
: don't *think* about what they doing, and what its effect will be.

Do you really think it's possible to know beforehand?

[From "Some Principles Of History"]

103. THIRD PRINCIPLE.  If a change is made that is large enough to
alter permanently a long-term trend, then the consequences for the
society as a whole cannot be predicted in advance. [...]

104. FOURTH PRINCIPLE.  A new kind of society cannot be designed on
paper.  That is, you cannot plan out a new form of society in advance,
then set it up and expect it to function as it was designed to.

105. The third and fourth principles result from the complexity of human
societies.  A change in human behavior will affect the economy of a
society and its physical environment; the economy will effect the
environment and vice versa, and the changes in the economy and the
environment will affect human behavior in complex, unpredictable ways;
and so forth.  The network of causes and effects is far too complex to
be untangled and understood.

106. FIFTH PRINCIPLE.  People do not consciously and rationally choose the
form of their society.  Societies develop through processes of social
evolution that are not under rational human control.

: Yeah, I've heard some horror stories from friends.  Stuff that I
: wouldn't put up with, and stuff they *didn't* put up with.  The
: problem in this society is that so many people don't have a *choice*
: about that.  Some of us are lucky and have skills in industries where
: there is currently a large need for workers, but it really stinks that
: others are locked into a job where they are miserable.

So is capitalism from the worker's perspective better or worse than
slavery?  On one hand you are "free" to choose your master, but on
the other, the money you are given goes for food and shelter that
slavemasters would have previously covered.  Granted slavery was
inhumane in its treatment of workers, but is capitalism anything
more than a humane and complicated form of distributed slavery?
